options.why: Counted $85^{\circ}+95^{\circ}$ and $110^{\circ}+70^{\circ}$ as two different pairs of parallel sides, when both tests give the same pair.

options.text: $x=35$ and no pair of sides is parallel, so $ABCD$ is an ordinary quadrilateral.
options.why: Tested only $\angle DAB+\angle CDA=155^{\circ}$ and concluded nothing was parallel without testing the other transversal.

questions.solution_text:
$85+95+(3x+5)+2x=360$ (angle sum of a quadrilateral)
$5x+185=360$
$5x=175$
$x=35$
$\angle BCD=3(35)+5=110^{\circ}$ and $\angle CDA=2(35)=70^{\circ}$
$\angle DAB+\angle ABC=85^{\circ}+95^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$, so $AD\parallel BC$ (co-interior angles on the transversal $AB$)
$\angle BCD+\angle CDA=110^{\circ}+70^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$, which tests the same pair on the transversal $DC$
$\angle DAB+\angle CDA=85^{\circ}+70^{\circ}=155^{\circ}$, so $AB$ is not parallel to $DC$ (co-interior angles do not add to $180^{\circ}$)
Only one pair of sides is parallel, so $ABCD$ is a trapezium.

$\triangle ABC$ has $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=2y$, and $BC$ is produced to $D$.
Which expression gives $\angle ACD$?

options.why: Gave the interior angle $\angle ACB$ rather than the exterior angle $\angle ACD$ beside it.
Subtracted the apex angle from $180^{\circ}$ without halving to find each of the two equal base angles.
Used the exterior angle theorem with the apex angle alone, leaving out $\angle ABC$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC=\angle ACB$ (base angles of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$)
$\angle ACB=(180^{\circ}-2y)\div2=90^{\circ}-y$ (angle sum of a triangle)
$\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-(90^{\circ}-y)$ (angles on the straight line $BCD$)
$=90^{\circ}+y$

$a^{\circ}$, $b^{\circ}$ and $c^{\circ}$ are the reflex angles at the three vertices of the triangle.
What is the value of $a+b+c$?

options.why: Used $3\times360$ for the three full turns but did not subtract the interior angles of the triangle.
Subtracted $360$, the angle sum of a quadrilateral, from $3\times360$ instead of subtracting the triangle's angle sum of $180$.
Gave the sum of the three interior angles instead of the three reflex angles.

questions.solution_text:
Let the interior angles of the triangle be $p^{\circ}$, $q^{\circ}$ and $r^{\circ}$.
$a+p=360$, $b+q=360$ and $c+r=360$ (angles at a point)
$a+b+c+p+q+r=1080$
$p+q+r=180$ (angle sum of a triangle)
$a+b+c=1080-180$
$=900$
